circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281-kilometre track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has been home to Formula One's season finale since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern venue for the sport, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne that hosts the annual Australian Grand Prix and various supporting motorsport events. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and serves as a premier destination for international racing competitions.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit originally opened as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following a reconstruction and shortening, the track was later renamed and resumed hosting the national Grand Prix from 1997 through 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street-based racing venue in Azerbaijan's capital, measuring 6. 003 kilometers per lap and ranking as the fourth-longest on the F1 calendar. The venue first hosted a Formula One race in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming a permanent fixture on the schedule a year later under the Azerbaijan Grand Prix designation.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix ever held in the Middle East that same year. Beyond its primary F1 event, the track accommodates various motorsport competitions including drag racing, GP2 Series, and endurance racing, while operating under FIA Grade 1 classification with multiple configurable layouts.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometer Spanish circuit features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of overall racing performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit situated in the Wallonian region near Stavelot that has served as the home of the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1925. The track hosted a race during F1's inaugural season in 1950 and has been a consistent fixture on the calendar annually from 1985 onward, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361 km street circuit serves as the home of the Canadian Grand Prix in Formula One racing. Beyond Formula One, the venue has attracted various international motorsport series including sports car championships, open-wheel racing, and NASCAR competitions over its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit, located in the Jiading District of Shanghai, is a motorsport facility renowned for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue also began staging the Shanghai ePrix electric racing championship in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, this English racing venue has hosted the British Grand Prix since 1948 and was the site of the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After alternating with two other circuits from 1955 to 1986, it became the permanent home of the British Grand Prix and continues to serve as a major racing facility for multiple motorsport series.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted Formula One's first Grand Prix held in a Soviet bloc nation when it opened in 1986. Built remarkably quickly in just eight months after construction began in late 1985, the track was established outside the city alongside a major highway rather than as a street circuit in Budapest's central park as initially proposed.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza, a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 near Milan, ranks among Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venues and is celebrated as "the Temple of Speed" for its extended straights and fast-cornering sections. The track has continuously hosted Italy's premier Formula One event since 1949, aside from a 1980 closure for renovation work.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda's Mobilityland subsidiary, hosting up to 155,000 spectators. The track is renowned primarily for hosting Formula One races and Super Formula championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, weaving around the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its collection of world-renowned casinos and hotels. The track incorporates iconic landmarks such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it winds through the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is named in tribute to two racing brothers who died in separate accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix in multiple eras, most recently from 2015 onwards on its current layout, after a 23-year absence from the calendar.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary track constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that allows qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Developed by specialist circuit designers Apex Circuit Design, the venue was built specifically to host the Miami Grand Prix, which debuted on the Formula One calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the urban areas of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, encircling Monaco's harbour. Though officially named after the principality itself, the circuit is widely known as "Monte Carlo" due to its primary location within that particular district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch dunes near the North Sea, approximately 35 kilometers west of Amsterdam, this 4. 259-kilometer circuit hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after returning to Formula One's schedule in 2021. The venue's involvement in the championship concluded following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is situated near Lusail, north of Doha in Qatar, and features a 5. 419 km layout with a 1. 068 km main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, a 4. 309 km circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise track features an on-site kart facility dedicated to another celebrated Brazilian racing driver, Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: A street circuit situated along Jeddah's waterfront promenade beside the Red Sea, this Saudi Arabian venue has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural 2021 running. The track also began welcoming Formula E competition from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: Marina Bay Street Circuit is an urban racing venue in Singapore that winds around the Marina Bay waterfront, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657-kilometre circuit in Montmeló features a balanced combination of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple driving skills. The track, which holds an FIA Grade 1 classification, accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major international motorsport events including MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas and the FIA World Endurance Championship's Lone Star Le Mans, along with NASCAR competition.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British motorsport competitor who currently races for Williams, representing Thailand in Formula One competition.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 plus 32 Grand Prix victories across 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours wins with Toyota and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both a Formula One title and a world sportscar championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian driver, made his Formula One debut in 2025 with Mercedes, where he currently competes. He has already secured seven Grand Prix victories during his early career in the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British racing driver currently competing in Formula One for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto, a Brazilian motorsport competitor, currently drives in Formula One representing Audi in the championship series.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that includes ten race victories. He achieved his strongest championship results while with Mercedes, securing runner-up finishes in both 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine, representing his country in the sport's top racing series.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan races in the European Le Mans Series with Nielsen Racing while holding a reserve role at Haas in Formula One, where he has participated in seven Grand Prix events during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French motorsport competitor, currently drives for Alpine in Formula One. He previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while representing AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a Franco-Algerian racing driver representing France in Formula One, currently driving for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: British driver Lewis Hamilton competes for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured seven World Drivers' Championship titles that equal Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple sport records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg, a German driver, currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved success in endurance competition, notably securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand-born racing driver, currently races for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver currently racing for Ferrari, finished as championship runner-up in 2022 and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT as a BMW factory driver, while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career with Trackhouse Racing. His Formula One career spanned two separate periods, running from 2014 to 2020 before returning for the 2022 and 2023 seasons.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver competing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship title. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has secured 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The driver previously achieved victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez is a Mexican driver competing in Formula One for Cadillac, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. The seasoned competitor finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull and has claimed six race victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver competing for McLaren, has claimed nine Formula One victories throughout his four-season career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", competed in Formula One over fourteen years between 2011 and 2024, securing victories in eight Grand Prix races during his career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four race victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant, an American driver, competed in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following previous stints in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, competing under his commonly used name rather than his full surname Strulovitch.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, holds a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls after competing as a full-time Formula One competitor from 2021 through 2025. He transitioned to a backup role beginning in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen, a Dutch and Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing, has secured four consecutive World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Over his 12-season Formula One career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu remains the sole Chinese competitor to have raced in Formula One, having driven in the series between 2022 and 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based outfit has operated under the Alpine banner since 2021, serving as Renault's factory team during this period. Originally established as Renault F1 Team, the squad was rebranded to showcase the French manufacturer's Alpine sports car marque, maintaining direct works status until Renault's withdrawal from the championship at season's end in 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has been a recurring presence in Formula One across multiple eras, with its contemporary involvement structured through AMR GP Limited and competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari in Formula One competition. As motorsport's longest-running and most accomplished team, it has participated in every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950, earning the affectionate nickname "the Prancing Horse" from its distinctive emblem.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: The American-licensed team was founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014 and entered Formula One competition in 2016. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, Ayao Komatsu assumed the role of team principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering firm established itself through endurance racing success before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. The team competed in the sport for over three decades through various iterations, becoming the fourth-longest-running constructor by race count before transitioning to Audi's works program in 2025.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under sponsorship arrangements in the championship. The organisation operates as part of the McLaren Group and is ultimately owned by Bahraini investment company Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current team based in Brackley and operating under a German racing licence. Since January 2022, ownership has been shared equally among Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. The team's vehicles carry the iconic "Silver Arrows" designation, reflecting decades of Mercedes' motorsport heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the championship in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Operating from Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the team functions as the energy drink conglomerate's second racing entity in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that entered the championship in 2024 as Red Bull's second factory operation. Based in Faenza with a supporting facility in Milton Keynes, the team operates alongside Red Bull Racing as part of the Austrian conglomerate's dual-team structure in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing operates as an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and owned by Red Bull GmbH, which also operates Racing Bulls in the sport. Established in 2005 and managed by Christian Horner until his 2025 departure, the team has become one of the championship's prominent competitors under Laurent Mekies' leadership.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, operating as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. The team maintains its headquarters at a substantial facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, and has remained a fixture in the sport since its inception.
